title: Wheels, rims and hubs
summary: See how the tire, rim, spokes and hub form one load-bearing wheel system and where rotation actually happens.

steps.title: A wheel is several jobs in one.
steps.body: The tire contacts the road, the rim supports the tire, spokes transfer load, and the hub provides the rotating center.
steps.keyFact: Treating a wheel as one object hides the very different jobs performed by its parts.

steps.title: The rim carries tire loads into the spoke structure.
steps.body: The rim must stay round, support the tire and distribute local road forces around the wheel. Stiffness, mass and shape all affect how the wheel behaves.
steps.keyFact: The rim is not the rotating bearing surface; that job belongs at the hub.

steps.title: Rotation is concentrated at the hub.
steps.body: The hub houses the axle and bearings. The wheel rotates around that bearing system while the axle locates the wheel in the frame.
steps.keyFact: Good wheel rotation depends heavily on bearing condition, adjustment and alignment at the hub.

steps.title: Find the hub.
steps.body: Use the 3D model or the accessible choices below to identify the part that contains the wheel bearings and sits at the wheel center.
steps.keyFact: The hub is the wheel's central rotating assembly.

challenge.prompt: Which component contains the wheel bearings?
challenge.successText: Correct. The hub sits at the wheel center and houses the bearing system.
challenge.retryText: That part belongs to the wheel, but it is not the bearing housing. Look toward the center.
